account: Julie Knichel, a 57-year-old nurse, suffered a ruptured brain aneurysm. At Baptist Health's Marcus Neuroscience Institute, AI reviewed her scan and alerted clinicians to the bleeding. They sealed the aneurysm with coils delivered through a catheter. After about three weeks in hospital, she recovered and returned to full-time nursing. Her symptoms began on 2 February 2024. Baptist Health gives the day and month, and Jan Engoren’s subsequent interviews with Knichel and Snelling establish the year. The surgeon names Viz.ai in a later interview and describes an unnamed ICU nurse whose circumstances match Knichel’s. The product attribution is therefore inferred. Neither account identifies the module or release.

ai_role.statement: AI flagged the bleeding and notified the stroke team, according to her treating surgeon. Clinicians treated the aneurysm. Viz.ai is an inferred identification from his separate interview. The sources do not isolate the software’s effect on survival.

claim_basis: Sources: two independent news reports, the makers' report, the deployer's report and the deployer's news report. The cited evidence includes no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.

fields.account: Julie Knichel, a 57-year-old nurse, suffered a ruptured brain aneurysm. At Baptist Health's Marcus Neuroscience Institute, AI reviewed her scan and alerted clinicians to the bleeding. They sealed the aneurysm with coils delivered through a catheter. After about three weeks in hospital, she recovered and returned to full-time nursing. Her symptoms began on 2 February 2024. Baptist Health gives the day and month, and Jan Engoren’s subsequent interviews with Knichel and Snelling establish the year. The surgeon names Viz.ai in a later interview and describes an unnamed ICU nurse whose circumstances match Knichel’s. The product attribution is therefore inferred. Neither account identifies the module or release.
